title: The I-power torsion submodule is unchanged by a flat base change that is an isomorphism modulo I
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a flat ring map of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $I\subseteq R$ a finitely generated ideal such that the ring map $R/I\to S/IS$ induced by $\varphi$ is an isomorphism ($IS$ the ideal of $S$ generated by $\varphi(I)$). For an $R$-module $P$ put $P[I^\infty]=\{x\in P:\ I^nx=0\text{ for some }n\ge1\}$, a submodule of $P$. Let $M$ be an $R$-module and $M\otimes_RS$ its base change [def-weil-module-base-change], regarded as an $R$-module via $\varphi$ (so $(M\otimes_RS)[I^\infty]$ is the set of $y$ with $I^ny=0$ for some $n$, equivalently $(IS)^ny=0$, since $(IS)^n$ is generated by $\varphi(I^n)$). Then $m\mapsto m\otimes1$ maps $M[I^\infty]$ into $(M\otimes_RS)[I^\infty]$, and the resulting map $M[I^\infty]\to(M\otimes_RS)[I^\infty]$ is bijective.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05EC (lemma-neighbourhood-equivalence, line 24301), part (1)

proof.text: (The map is defined.) For $x\in M$ and $a\in R$ we have $a(x\otimes1)=ax\otimes1$ in $M\otimes_RS$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. Hence if $I^nx=0$ then $I^n(x\otimes1)=0$, so $\psi:M[I^\infty]\to(M\otimes_RS)[I^\infty]$, $\psi(x)=x\otimes1$, is a well-defined $R$-linear map. (That $P[I^\infty]$ is a submodule: if $I^ax=0$ and $I^by=0$ then $I^{\max(a,b)}(x+y)=0$ and $I^a(rx)=0$.)

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05EC (lemma-neighbourhood-equivalence, line 24301), proof of part (1), the map M -> M (x) S of the statement

proof.text: (The quotient has no $I$-power torsion.) Put $T=M[I^\infty]$ and $M'=M/T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-by-power-torsion-no-torsion] ($I$ is finitely generated) $M'[I]=0$. By induction on $n\ge1$, $M'[I^n]=0$: the case $n=1$ is that statement; if $n\ge2$ and $I^n\bar x=0$, then every $\bar y=a\bar x$ with $a\in I^{n-1}$ satisfies $I\bar y\subseteq I^n\bar x=0$, so $\bar y\in M'[I]=0$; thus $I^{n-1}\bar x=0$ and $\bar x=0$ by induction. Hence $M'[I^\infty]=0$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05EC (lemma-neighbourhood-equivalence, line 24301), proof of part (1): 'By Lemma 05EB we see that M'[I^infty] = 0' (the passage from M'[I]=0 to M'[I^n]=0 is Lemma 05EA (lemma-torsion-free), (1) => (2), written out here)

proof.text: (A test map.) Write $I=(f_1,\dots,f_t)$. Fix $n\ge1$ and let $\delta:M'\to M'^{\,t}=\prod_{k=1}^tM'$, $\bar x\mapsto(f_1^n\bar x,\dots,f_t^n\bar x)$. Then $\delta$ is injective: if $f_k^n\bar x=0$ for all $k$, then $I^{t(n-1)+1}\bar x=0$, because $I^{t(n-1)+1}$ is generated by the monomials $f_1^{e_1}\cdots f_t^{e_t}$ with $e_1+\dots+e_t=t(n-1)+1$, and in each of them some $e_k\ge n$ (otherwise the sum is at most $t(n-1)$), so the monomial is a multiple of $f_k^n$; hence $\bar x\in M'[I^\infty]=0$ by step 2. (If $t=0$, $I=0$, $M'[I]=M'=0$ and everything below is trivial.)

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05EC (lemma-neighbourhood-equivalence, line 24301), proof of part (1): 'Hence for every n > 0 the map M' -> (+)_{i=1..t} M', x -> (f_1^n x, ..., f_t^n x) is injective' (the pigeonhole bound is written out here)

proof.text: (Base change of the test map.) Since $\varphi$ is flat, $\delta\otimes1:M'\otimes_RS\to M'^{\,t}\otimes_RS$ is injective [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Compose with the isomorphism $\pi:M'^{\,t}\otimes_RS\to\prod_{k}(M'\otimes_RS)$, $(x_k)_k\otimes s\mapsto(x_k\otimes s)_k$ [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-finite-product]. On pure tensors $\pi(\delta\otimes1)(\bar x\otimes s)=(f_k^n\bar x\otimes s)_k=(f_k^n(\bar x\otimes s))_k$ [def-weil-module-base-change]; both $\pi\circ(\delta\otimes1)$ and $y\mapsto(f_1^ny,\dots,f_t^ny)$ are additive and pure tensors generate $M'\otimes_RS$, so they are equal, and $y\mapsto(f_k^ny)_k$ is injective on $M'\otimes_RS$. Now if $y\in(M'\otimes_RS)$ and $I^ny=0$ for some $n\ge1$, then $f_k^ny=0$ for all $k$ (as $f_k^n\in I^n$), so $y=0$. Hence $(M'\otimes_RS)[I^\infty]=0$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05EC (lemma-neighbourhood-equivalence, line 24301), proof of part (1): 'As S is flat over R also the corresponding map M' (x) S -> (+) M' (x) S is injective. This means that (M' (x)_R S)[I^n] = 0 as desired.'

proof.text: (The base-changed sequence.) Let $\iota:T\to M$ be the inclusion and $q:M\to M'$ the projection, so $0\to T\to M\to M'\to0$ is exact. Tensoring with $S$: $\iota\otimes1:T\otimes_RS\to M\otimes_RS$ is injective because $\varphi$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and $T\otimes_RS\to M\otimes_RS\to M'\otimes_RS\to0$ is exact [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact]. So $0\to T\otimes_RS\to M\otimes_RS\to M'\otimes_RS\to0$ is exact.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05EC (lemma-neighbourhood-equivalence, line 24301), proof of part (1): the exact sequence 0 -> M[I^infty] -> M -> M' -> 0 and the reduction 'it suffices to show that (M' (x)_R S)[(IS)^infty] = 0', which uses this sequence after base change

proof.text: (The torsion part is unchanged.) $T=M[I^\infty]$ is an $I$-power torsion $R$-module (each element is killed by a power of $I$). Since $\varphi$ is flat and $R/I\to S/IS$ is an isomorphism, the map $T\to T\otimes_RS$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, is bijective [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-module-flat-base-change-iso].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05EC (lemma-neighbourhood-equivalence, line 24301), proof of part (1): 'As M[I^infty] = M[I^infty] (x)_R S' (Lemma 05E9, whose hypotheses hold as the proof notes at its start: an isomorphism R/I -> S/IS is faithfully flat, so the conditions of 05E7 hold)

proof.text: (Conclusion.) The map $\psi$ of step 1 is the composite $T\to T\otimes_RS\xrightarrow{\iota\otimes1}M\otimes_RS$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1\mapsto x\otimes1$, with values in $(M\otimes_RS)[I^\infty]$. Injective: a composite of the bijection of step 6 and the injection of step 5. Surjective: let $y\in M\otimes_RS$ with $I^ny=0$. Then $(q\otimes1)(y)$ is killed by $I^n$, so it is $0$ by step 4; by exactness in step 5, $y=(\iota\otimes1)(z)$ with $z\in T\otimes_RS$; by step 6, $z=x\otimes1$ with $x\in T$; so $y=x\otimes1=\psi(x)$. Hence $\psi:M[I^\infty]\to(M\otimes_RS)[I^\infty]$ is bijective.
